title: Animals and nature
goal: By the end of this lesson you can name common animals, landscapes and outdoor activities, and talk about a weekend at the chalet in Quebec.

body: Pets (*les animaux de compagnie*): *le chien*, *le chat*, *le poisson*, *l'oiseau* (m). Note the irregular plurals: *un animal* → *des animaux*, *un oiseau* → *des oiseaux*.

Wild animals of Quebec: *l'orignal* (moose), *l'ours* (bear), *le castor* (beaver), *le loup* (wolf), *le renard* (fox), *le raton laveur* (raccoon), *l'écureuil* (squirrel), *le huard* (loon), *la bernache* (Canada goose).
Some animal names are always masculine or always feminine whatever the animal's sex: *une souris* (a mouse), *un écureuil*, *une girafe*. Add *mâle* or *femelle* if needed.
learn.tip: Most nouns in -al make their plural in -aux: un orignal, des orignaux.

body: *la forêt* (forest), *le bois* (woods), *la montagne* (mountain), *le lac* (lake), *la rivière* (river), *le fleuve* (a large river flowing to the sea, like *le fleuve Saint-Laurent*), *la plage* (beach), *l'île* (f, island), *le champ* (field).
Prepositions: *dans la forêt*, *au bord du lac* (at the lakeside), *sur la montagne* or *à la montagne* (in the mountains), *au bord de l'eau*.
*Le fleuve* vs *la rivière*: Quebecers always say *le fleuve* for the Saint Lawrence because it flows into the sea.

*aller à la pêche* or *faire de la pêche* (to go fishing), *faire du camping*, *faire de la randonnée* (to hike), *faire du canot* (to go canoeing; *canot* is the Quebec word, France says *canoë*), *faire un feu de camp* (to make a campfire).
Use *faire de* + activity and the partitive: *du camping*, *de la randonnée*, *du kayak*. In the passé composé: *On a fait du canot toute la journée.*

In Quebec, *un chalet* is a cottage or cabin in the country, often by a lake. *Aller au chalet* is a classic Quebec weekend. In France a *chalet* suggests a mountain house; the Quebec meaning is much broader.
Typical chalet life: *se baigner dans le lac* (to swim in the lake), *pêcher la truite* (to fish for trout), *faire un feu*, *regarder les étoiles*, and fighting *les maringouins* (mosquitoes).

quebec.intro: Nature is central to Quebec life: the chalet, fishing and the orignal (moose) are everyday topics, and a few animal and outdoor words are Quebec-specific.

dialogue.fr: Puis, ton week-end au chalet, c'était comment?
dialogue.en: So, how was your weekend at the cottage?

dialogue.fr: Super! On a fait du canot sur le lac samedi matin.
dialogue.en: Great! We went canoeing on the lake Saturday morning.

dialogue.fr: Oui, un orignal et deux huards. Et beaucoup trop de maringouins!

dialogue.fr: Chanceux! Vous avez fait un feu?

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about a perfect weekend in nature: where, with whom, what you do, what animals you see.
write.model: Mon week-end idéal, c'est au chalet dans les Laurentides. J'y vais avec mes amis. Le matin, on fait du canot sur le lac. L'après-midi, on fait de la randonnée dans la forêt. Le soir, on fait un feu de camp. Avec un peu de chance, on voit un orignal ou un castor.
